feedback: Approve. The candidate is valid: mass 0.6 is inside the 0.4 to 1.5 contract range, and every other field matches the best raced design (iteration 7, score 687.06). It changes one variable that no earlier iteration has tested, since mass has been 0.8 in every raced design. The yaw-inertia reasoning is sound (inertia = mass*(L^2+W^2)/12), and the slalom's sign changes are where lag matters most. Gain and geometry levers are already exhausted: kp 4.0 cut slalom progress (iteration 5), kd 0.8 cut it while helping the s-bend (iteration 4), narrowing spacing to ±0.02 m lost ground (iteration 9, 676.7), and the 16 mm footprint was neutral (iteration 8, 685.5). Approving now gives the team a race on a new lever, and a result either way sharpens iteration 11. Compare the result with iteration 7 per track: slalom progress and max_error first, then oval finish count and s-bend steering_oscillation. Next step, depending on the result: if the score is at or above 687 with the oval at 19/20 or better, keep mass 0.6 and test mass 0.5 as the single change, since lower inertia is the direction that helped. If the score falls below 687, or the oval drops to 18/20 or below, or s-bend steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.37, revert to the iteration 7 design exactly (mass 0.8) and do not adjust gains to rescue it. Keep ki at 0, base_speed at 1.3 and line_loss at last_direction.
